data.title: Bitmine Chair Tom Lee Says Crypto Market Could Rise Even If CLARITY Act Fails
data.description:
Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee said in an interview that the crypto market could keep rising even if the CLARITY Act does not pass. According to Odaily, Lee said market demand matters more than any single bill, and that the CLARITY Act was intended to create a clearer regulatory framework for the crypto industry and give the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission more defined oversight duties.

Lee added that even if the bill fails, the SEC and the CFTC would remain the main federal regulators for the crypto industry. He also pointed to prediction markets and sports markets as examples of sectors that have continued to grow despite regulatory uncertainty.

data.title: StubHub Gains After Citi Upgrade, Higher App Download Forecast
data.description: According to CNBC, StubHub shares rose 3.8% on Friday after Citi upgraded the ticket reselling platform to buy from neutral. Analyst Jason Bazinet cut his price target to $7 from $9, but said that still implies 18% upside from Thursday's close. Bazinet said he expects StubHub's adjusted EBITDA to beat analyst estimates and full-year earnings to land near the top end of company guidance, helped by record weekly app downloads during the World Cup and higher downloads since then. He also forecast $10.9 billion in gross merchandise sales for 2026, above the company's guidance, and said StubHub had about 40% market share in online ticket resale. StubHub stock is down 51% year to date.

data.title: AI | Torsten Slok Says AI Spending Has Been Critical for the US Economy
data.description:
AI hardware continued to drive August's increase in import prices, as it has throughout the year, while commodity-price volatility from the Iran war lifted the cost of industrial materials at the border, according to Bloomberg.

Companies are facing higher input costs and rising expenses tied to the AI buildout. Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo Global Management, discussed the Fed's rate decision and said AI investment has played a role in supporting the US economy.

data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey R. Schmid said he supports the FOMC raising rates in September and that inflation is not limited to the energy sector.

data.title: STOCKS | California Governor Newsom Issues Order to Advance AI Oversight
data.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom issued an executive order aimed at accelerating independent oversight of artificial intelligence and promoting an AI "emergency shutdown" mechanism. According to Sina Finance, the governor's office said the statement called for nationwide adoption of California's AI framework.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Auto Industry Presses Trump to Block Chinese Carmakers From US
data.description:
A broad coalition of automakers, suppliers and dealers is urging US President Donald Trump to keep Chinese cars out of the US, according to Bloomberg.

The appeal comes ahead of a planned summit between the US and China next week that could include a role for Chinese electric-vehicle giant BYD Co.

data.title: Samsung Wallet Lists Stablecoins as a Payment Partnership Area in New York Job Posting
data.description: Samsung Electronics America is hiring a senior manager for Samsung Wallet payment business development in New York, and the posting lists stablecoins as a payment partnership area alongside card issuers, payment companies, fintech firms, and buy now, pay later services. According to Odaily, the role will cover Samsung Wallet payment business development, go-to-market strategy, and partner management, including negotiations over commercial terms, data use, product requirements, and new feature launches. Samsung previously said at its Galaxy Unpacked event in July that Samsung Wallet would support stablecoins in the future.

data.title: Glassnode Says Altcoin Leverage Remains Below Risk Threshold
data.description: Glassnode said on X that altcoin leverage levels remain below the risk threshold. According to Odaily, the firm said markets are usually overheated when the gap between altcoin open interest share and Bitcoin narrows to within a few percentage points, and that condition has not yet occurred.

data.title: Haruko Suffers Targeted Cyberattack, Affecting 15 Clients
data.description:
London-based crypto technology services provider Haruko was hit by a targeted cyberattack this week, affecting 15 clients and allegedly causing asset losses for some smaller hedge fund customers. Trading data was also stolen. According to Foresight News, the attacker exploited a vulnerability in Haruko's infrastructure to extract user access tokens and obtain read-only exchange API information and other data stored in process memory, while customer login credentials were not affected.

Haruko co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Adam Carlile said the attack was directed at Haruko itself. He added that the vulnerability has been fixed, server keys have been refreshed, and a full technical postmortem will be released. Haruko's website lists clients including Bitcoin Suisse, GSR, and Flowdesk, and GSR said it was not affected.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | EU Scrutinizes Amazon Over Suspected Seller Price Restrictions
data.description:
Amazon.com Inc. is under scrutiny from the European Union over potential unfair restrictions on firms selling on its platform, according to Bloomberg.

The review centers on suspected price curbs on sellers using Amazon's marketplace.

data.title: Trader Bonk Guy Says USELESS Has Formed a Large Cup-and-Handle Pattern
data.description: Trader Bonk Guy said USELESS is showing very strong momentum and has formed a large cup-and-handle pattern over the past year. According to Odaily, he said the last similar setup he saw was BONK in late 2023, which rose more than 1,600% in the weeks after breaking out. Bonk Guy added that USELESS is his highest-conviction meme coin and said it could become the first meme coin in this cycle to reach a market value above $10 billion.

data.title: Repo Borrowing Costs Rise as Treasury Yields Surge
data.description:
The cost to borrow key short-term Treasuries is rising as investors buy recently issued securities to establish short positions, according to Bloomberg.

The move could support next week’s US government debt auctions.

data.title: BMO Upgrades MACOM Technology Solutions to Outperform, Sees 27% Upside
data.description: According to CNBC, BMO Capital Markets upgraded MACOM Technology Solutions to outperform from market perform and kept its price target at $335 per share, implying 27% upside from Thursday's close. Analyst Harsh Kumar said valuations have become attractive as forward multiples fell from the high-50s in June to 29x, and said fundamentals have stayed solid on demand from datacenter and industrial/defense markets, with defense resilient and space becoming a material growth contributor next year. The bank said MACOM's data center business could benefit as hyperscalers, cloud service providers and AI labs direct more spending toward AI compute and networking infrastructure. It also said revenue from the data center vertical is expected to grow 70% in fiscal 2026, after a 47% increase in the prior fiscal year. Shares of MACOM have fallen about 30% over the past three months and trade more than 30% below their late-May peak of $418.90. LSEG data show 13 of 18 analysts covering MACOM rate the stock buy or strong buy, while five rate it hold.

data.title: Yahoo Finance Ends Prediction Market Partnership With Polymarket
data.description:
Yahoo Finance has ended its prediction market partnership with Polymarket, which was reached in November last year. According to Foresight News, Polymarket data had been displayed exclusively on Yahoo Finance for probabilities tied to economic, government, and market forecasts, but the section was taken offline in April this year.

Yahoo said Polymarket remains an advertising partner and that similar cooperation is still possible. Polymarket declined to comment.

data.title: Chip Roy Says Congress Should Hear From AI CEOs on Safety Concerns
data.description: According to CNBC, U.S. Representative Chip Roy said Congress has an oversight role in artificial intelligence but does not need to regulate the technology. Speaking on "Squawk Box," the Texas Republican said he does not want to regulate anything and instead favors AI chief executives testifying at congressional hearings to explain what they are doing to address safety concerns. Roy said Congress has a role in asking companies what they are doing about a technology that is so pervasive, and he added that he is not an AI "doomer."
